title: Establish residency triage runbook and prioritization rubric for new-region & failover requests
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Create a concise, actionable triage runbook and scoring rubric for customer requests touching region availability, data residency constraints, and failover requirements. Scope includes: intake form fields, initial validation checklist, impact scoring (compliance risk, latency/customer SLA, cost & capacity), recommended next steps (blocker, needs-legal, quick-accept, scope-for-PI), and owner handoffs (PM -> Infra -> Security -> Solutions).
acceptance_criteria: Public triage runbook (Confluence) exists and is linked from the intake form
A prioritization rubric with numerical scoring (0-10) for: compliance risk, customer revenue/strategic value, latency impact, operational effort, and deployment dependency
A one-click intake form template (Google Form + auto Slack notify) for Solutions and Sales to use
Clear routing matrix: when to route to Dedicated, Private, or Hosted with fallbacks and stubbed timelines
Two example triaged customer requests documented end-to-end (one high-compliance, one failover-only) demonstrating runbook application
notes: Common request patterns: (A) new geography for data residency, (B) cross-region failover for high availability, (C) strict residency for regulated PII workloads

Initial data points to collect: customer org size, specific regulatory requirement (e.g., EU GDPR article reference, APAC local law), expected RPS and percent of traffic to region, SLA expectations, contracted revenue
Operational constraints: Dedicated capacity procurement lead time (~4-6 weeks), Private deployments require security sign-off and infra resources, hosting in new region may need partner contracts
Cost estimation guidelines: quick estimate ranges for single-region low-latency (<50ms) vs isolated residency (VPC + dedicated GPUs) — include model size multipliers
Legal/Compliance: map common residency asks to SEC/Privacy team owners and required artifacts (DPA, SCCs or local adequacy proof)
Fallbacks: encourage multi-tier approach — preferred region -> fallback region list -> public-hosted degrade mode (with consent)
